scope: App cards guide and AEO MDX only, plus progress documentation. Other six bodies/dates/schema objects and shared templates/fonts unchanged.
skills: Corey Haines copy-editing, mode B, seven sweeps and final checklist
Existing product marketing context and Tom Voice compass
Blog-factcheck for technical claims, research scope, packaging and dates
constraints: Compact English personal portfolio, conversations welcome without project-capacity promises. No new marketing sections, stock imagery, invented experience or outcome guarantee.

copy_checks.clarity: Distinguishes native record cards from app-provided UI extensions. AEO describes tracked visibility, citations and site visits as different observations.
copy_checks.voice: Practical first-person recommendations with concrete actions. Removes unverified client anecdote, we-language and automatic payback assertions.
copy_checks.so_what: Starts from a record decision or buyer question. Explains access/maintenance and how tracking findings inform content work.
copy_checks.proof: Official HubSpot documentation for cards and AEO; primary Pew study for dated numbers; Google guidance limited to Google AI features. Actual renewal case preserves read-only and hosting boundaries.
copy_checks.specificity: Corrects app/native categories, layout versus installation, source freshness/matching, action failures, Sensitive Data restrictions, pricing/access differences and research denominators.
copy_checks.emotion: Recognizable repeated lookups and uncertainty about spending time on another tool; no traffic panic or cheap/easy-yes claims.
copy_checks.risk_and_expectations: Scope read-only view before write actions; test failures and name maintenance owner. AEO pilot has stable prompts, baseline and outcome/attribution limits; no citation or ranking guarantee.
copy_checks.final: No em dashes, duplicate takeaway/FAQ/conclusion, exposed citation capsule or broad sales ending. One compare-notes link per article; charts removed where they repeated the same figures.

app_cards: Native cards versus app cards; existing native/installed-app/custom options
Record, preview and help desk surfaces depend on app configuration
Example tasks distinguished from delivered capabilities
Matching, freshness, permissions, external connection and Sensitive Data restrictions
Testing outages, missing associations and repeated clicks; maintenance ownership
Classic-card source conflict and focused migration link
Compare custom cost and upkeep with actual repeated task
aeo: AEO definition and monitoring across supported engines
Mentions, citations, visits and leads measured separately
Dated Pew sample, traditional-result versus summary-link rates and observational limits
Current USD price, tax qualifier, standalone versus Marketing Hub packaging and free Grader distinction
Readable factual content and Google-specific eligibility with no special AI markup/inclusion promise
Stable buyer-language prompts, baseline and multi-day review
Referral/enquiry review and limits of attribution
Continue only when findings are useful and the team can act
